'''Neil Allison Campbell''' (April 17, 1946 – October 21, 2004) was an American scientist best known for his textbook, ''[[Campbell Biology]],'' first published in 1987. The textbook was significantly updated in subsequent editions by American biologists [[Jane Reece]] and [[Lisa Urry]], being used by over 700,000 students in both [[high school]] and [[college]]-level classes.<ref name="UC">{{cite press release
  | title = UC Riverside Visiting Scholar Dies
  | publisher = [[University of California, Riverside]]
  | date = 2004-10-25
  | url = http://www.newsroom.ucr.edu/cgi-bin/display.cgi?id=903
  | access-date = 2006-09-06
  | archive-date = 2008-10-13
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081013235620/http://www.newsroom.ucr.edu/cgi-bin/display.cgi?id=903
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref>

==Education==
Campbell earned his M.S. in [[zoology]] from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Plant Biology from the [[University of California, Riverside]]. He taught collegiate classes for over 30 years at [[Cornell University]], [[Pomona College]], [[University of California, Riverside]], and [[San Bernardino Valley College]].<ref>{{cite news
  | title = Neil A. Campbell; author of renowned biology text; 58
  | agency = [[Associated Press]]
  | pages = [[The San Diego Union-Tribune]]
  | date = 2004-11-02
  | url = http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20041102/news_1m2campbell.html
  | access-date = 2006-09-06 }}</ref>

==Work==
Campbell received multiple awards: the Distinguished Alumnus Award from [[University of California, Riverside]] in 2001 and the first ever Outstanding Professor Award from [[San Bernardino Valley College]] in 1986.<ref name="UC"/>

Campbell was also a researcher who studied desert and coastal plants. He conducted research on how certain plants would adjust in environments with different salinity, temperature, and pH. In addition, he conducted studies on the ''[[Mimosa]]'' plant and other legumes.<ref>{{cite book
  | last = Campbell
  | first = Neil A.
  | author2=Reece, Jane B. |author-link2=Jane B. Reece
  | title = Biology
  | url = https://archive.org/details/essentialbiology00camp_0
  | url-access = registration
  | publisher = [[Benjamin Cummings]]
  | year = 2005
  | isbn = 0-8053-7146-X
  | page = 1230 p }}</ref>

==Death==
Campbell died on 21 October 2004 of heart failure just after the manuscript for the seventh international edition of ''Biology'' was completed.<ref>{{cite news
  | last = Pearce
  | first = Jeremy
  | title = Neil A. Campbell, Who Wrote Major Biology Texts, Dies at 58
  | work = [[The New York Times]]
  | date = 2004-10-31
  | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2004/10/31/national/31campbell.html?ex=1157688000&en=198dfc9aee809bc3&ei=5070
  | access-date = 2006-09-06 }}</ref> The Neil Allison Campbell Endowed Research Award was created at UC Riverside to honor his memory.<ref>[https://advancementservices.ucr.edu/Scholarship/ScholarshipFundInfo.aspx?fund=600026 Neil Allison Campbell Endowed Research Award]</ref>
